findings.title: Redefining self.downsize overwrites the existing width/height API
findings.body: The class defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and then immediately defines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149. Ruby keeps only the second method. Existing callers using the old width/height form will now pass max_height as opts; optimize will then try to use opts[:allow_animation] or opts[:force_aspect_ratio] on an Integer/Fixnum (or use the wrong dimensions), causing downsizing to fail or behave incorrectly. Merge the two forms or update all callers.

findings.title: In-place downsize can leave an open tempfile pointing to the original bytes
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize runs an external command reading and writing tempfile.path while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. ImageMagick/gifsicle may replace the output by writing a temporary file and renaming over the destination; in that case the Ruby Tempfile file descriptor still refers to the old unlinked inode. The next tempfile.size call and Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ...) may then read the original, not the downsized image, defeating the size limit and possibly storing stale content. Write downsize output to a separate Tempfile/path and reopen or pass that file to Upload.create_for.

findings.title: Fixed five-attempt 80% loop does not guarantee the image is under max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The loop reduces the image to 80% of its current size per iteration and only runs attempt=5 times. That leaves the size at best 0.8^5 == 32.77% of the original. An image initially larger than about 3.05 times the configured limit remains above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes after the loop, but the code proceeds to Upload.create_for without checking downsize success or reporting the failure. Either iterate until the limit is met with a higher/calculated cap and check OptimizedImage.downsize's result, or reject with a clear error when the image cannot be reduced enough.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10 MB URL download cap bypasses configured upload limits for non-images
findings.body: The API URL download path now uses FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) instead of the configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The subsequent downsize block is only entered when FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is true, so non-image URL uploads can be downloaded at up to 10 MB even if the site's max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb is smaller. Keep the configured limit for non-images or validate the resulting upload against the site settings before creating it.

findings.title: Client-side upload size validation ignores site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile now sets maxSizeKB to a hardcoded 10 * 1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This allows users to select files up to 10 MB regardless of configured max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb, producing client behavior inconsistent with server policy and likely causing server-side 422/413 errors for normal attachments. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoded value; both should use the relevant site setting.

findings.title: No tests cover the new automatic downsize behavior
findings.body: This pull request adds a nontrivial server-side image mutation path but no controller/model tests. Cases that need coverage include an image over the limit being reduced below it, an image large enough that five 80% iterations are insufficient, an animated GIF when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and OptimizedImage.downsize returning false (e.g. ImageMagick/gifsicle missing or unsupported). Without these tests the in-place/stale file and fixed-attempt bugs are likely to regress unnoticed.
